title: Parallel circuits
body: In a parallel circuit each part has its own path, or branch, to the battery. Every branch gets the full battery voltage.
A battery gives a steady voltage, not a fixed current. Add a branch and the battery simply supplies more current. The total current is the sum of the branch currents.

So bulbs side by side each glow about as brightly as one bulb on its own. A real battery has a little resistance inside it, so each extra bulb dims them all slightly, and the battery runs down sooner.
realWorld: The sockets in your home are wired in parallel. Switching on a lamp doesn't make the TV dimmer.
